open_questions.text: For gig/self-employment income, does the $580 test use gross receipts (what the app paid) or net after expenses (mileage, gas, platform fees)? And is it 'gross income' or MAGI?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p7: 'total gross income'. No primary source addresses self-employment expenses. Secondary (Georgetown CCF on the IFR) describes MAGI-based income ('only taxable income sources, plus a few adjustments'), which for self-employment would normally be net. Primary and secondary may disagree.
open_questions.default_behavior: show both; flag if they disagree

open_questions.text: For rideshare/delivery, which hours count toward 80: logged-in/online time, or active (on-trip/engaged) time? Does waiting count?
open_questions.what_sources_say: Silent. ACWDL 25-30 p7 only says 'working at least 80 hours a month) including self-employment'. Implementation Plan p30 lists gig economy data (e.g., TRUV) as under assessment. Secondary (CCF) says hours can be converted from income using federal minimum wage; not in primary sources.
open_questions.default_behavior: show online hours and active hours separately; mark 'met' only if active hours >= 80; flag 'may count' if only online hours >= 80

open_questions.text: At application, is the look-back month the month before the APPLICATION month or before the DETERMINATION month? Could more than one month be used?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p9 and Implementation Plan p10: month before application. ACWDL 25-30 p11: month before the determination month. Secondary (CCF on IFR): states may use 1 to 3 consecutive months before application; California has not confirmed which in primary sources.
open_questions.default_behavior: assess the month before application as primary; also show the month before the expected determination month; encourage keeping proof for the 3 months before applying

open_questions.text: Exactly which months count at a six-month renewal (is the month of the last determination itself included? the renewal month?).
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p13: 'all months after the last determination and before the current renewal'. Examples: renewal due August -> February-July; due November -> May-October.
open_questions.default_behavior: use the 6 calendar months immediately before the renewal month, matching the examples; one compliant month is enough

open_questions.text: Can a gig driver with up-and-down income use the 6-month average, or is it only for 'seasonal' workers?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p7 says 'fluctuating income' (broad). Implementation Plan p11 says 'Seasonal employment'. Secondary (CCF): 'seasonal workers' with six-month average, or state may use reasonably predictable changes.
open_questions.default_behavior: always compute the 6-month average; show as a backup path labeled 'may count (rules unclear)'; never rely on it alone for a 'met' status

open_questions.text: If a month has income below $580 and hours below 80, can they be combined (e.g., convert dollars to hours at $7.25)?
open_questions.what_sources_say: Primary sources list combination only for work, work program, community service, and school hours (ACWDL 25-30 p8). Income is a separate test. No conversion stated. Secondary (CCF) mentions converting hours from income via minimum wage.
open_questions.default_behavior: do not combine income with hours; show 'short month' with how much more income ($) OR hours would meet the rule

open_questions.text: How many hours does half-time school count for in a combination month? Is it 'half-time' or 'part-time'?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p7 table: 'Go to school part-time or full-time'; p10 and Implementation Plan p11: 'at least half-time'. No hour value for school.
open_questions.default_behavior: treat half-time enrollment as meeting the month by itself; for combination, ask user for actual class/training hours and flag as unconfirmed

open_questions.text: After a Notice of Non-Compliance at application, can someone start working now to qualify?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p10: NNC 'is not intended as additional time to satisfy the requirement'. But p10-12 and p19 allow coverage to start the month after a later compliant month while the application is pending, and Step 3 lists 'Newly participate'. At renewal (p13) the 30 days are 'to come into compliance'.
open_questions.default_behavior: application: show proof for look-back month first; if none, show that new compliance starts coverage the 1st of the following month (earlier months lost). Renewal: show 30-day window to comply.

open_questions.text: Are high-unemployment county and federal disaster county mandatory exemptions or optional short-term hardships?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p3/p6 list them as exemptions; Implementation Plan p12 lists them as short-term hardships DHCS applies automatically.
open_questions.default_behavior: treat as automatic county-level checks the user cannot self-report; display as 'the county checks this'

open_questions.text: Does Alameda County (or a smaller local area) currently meet the high-unemployment test, and what geography counts?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p3: county rate at or above lesser of 8% or 1.5x national. Implementation Plan p12: 'county or local jurisdiction (not yet defined by CMS)'. No current rates in sources.
open_questions.default_behavior: assume not exempt; do not show as met

open_questions.text: What exactly counts as medically frail, and what proof is needed?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p5 lists categories; p26 says definition awaits CMS; Implementation Plan p12 fn 11: more info later.
open_questions.default_behavior: screen with plain question; route to 'possible exemption, ask county/doctor'; never auto-decide

open_questions.text: At application, which month must an exemption cover?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p11: exemption 'applies retroactively to the date of application'. Implementation Plan p10 fn 10: 'DHCS is seeking guidance from CMS on the timing for exemptions at application.'
open_questions.default_behavior: ask whether exemption applied in the look-back month or the application month; flag if only one

open_questions.text: What counts as a work program or community service?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p7: 'DHCS will provide additional guidance' for both.
open_questions.default_behavior: log hours with organization name and contact; flag as 'definition pending'

open_questions.text: Which documents will counties accept (e.g., Uber/Lyft/DoorDash earnings statements, 1099s, bank deposits)?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p20 and p26: acceptable forms of verification pending. Examples show pay stubs and sworn statement of enrollment.
open_questions.default_behavior: collect platform earnings statements plus a signed self-statement; label each as 'likely' not 'confirmed'

open_questions.text: For new applicants, is the first renewal at application month +5 or +6?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-31 p4 says 'six months from the first month of eligibility'; its p5 table puts it at +5 (January -> June). The transition table (p19) uses +6 (January renewal -> July).
open_questions.default_behavior: use the tables literally (new apps +5, transition +6) and tell the user to confirm the date on their notice

open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-31 p2 and Implementation Plan p13: effective January 1, 2027, with existing members transitioning at their first scheduled 2027 renewal. A DHCS changes page reportedly says March 1, 2027 (not verified; not in primary sources).
open_questions.default_behavior: use 2027-01-01 / first 2027 renewal; show a notice that DHCS may have changed this

open_questions.text: Will the $580 change if the federal minimum wage changes?
open_questions.what_sources_say: ACWDL 25-30 p7 ties it to federal minimum wage 'currently $7.25'. California's higher state minimum wage is not used.
open_questions.default_behavior: compute threshold = 80 x federal_minimum_wage_hourly from this config

open_questions.text: Have these preliminary ACWDLs been updated to match the June 2026 federal IFR?
open_questions.what_sources_say: Both ACWDLs say they are preliminary and subject to change. MEDIL I 26-25 (9/11/2026) exists but could not be read.
open_questions.default_behavior: show 'rules as of Dec 2025 state guidance' banner; re-check before demo

items.claim: Application look-back may be 1 to 3 consecutive months before application (state choice).
Income uses MAGI ('only taxable income sources, plus a few adjustments').
Seasonal workers: average monthly income over preceding six months, or state may use reasonably predictable changes.
If a state adopts short-term hardship, it must adopt all four events; disaster and unemployment applied automatically, inpatient and medical travel by request.
Self-attestation of medical frailty allowed in calendar year 2027 only; documentation when reasonably available from 2028-01-01.
Secretary may grant a state a good-faith exemption from the 2027-01-01 date, limited initially to six months.
